summary: Stanislav Šmelhaus (1887–1959) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. under Josef Zubatý around 1920–1925, and also studied at its First Faculty of Medicine and Faculty of Arts.

Stanisław Franciszek Michalski (1881–1961) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Warsaw, earned a Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder and Paul Kretschmer, and studied at Göttingen under Hermann Oldenberg and Jacob Wackernagel, later lecturing at the University of Łódź (1945–1960).

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Warsaw, Heidelberg, Freiburg (Ph.D. under Leumann and Husserl), Munich, and Lviv. He served at the University of Warsaw as director (1922), assistant professor (1929), and ordinarius professor (1938).
Stanley Abe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Cecil Sutton (1907–1993) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia, Tübingen under Karl Hoffmann, and Yale under Paul Thieme (Promotion c. 1963), later serving as Yale's Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology (c. 1980–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Ceylon and Cornell (Ph.D.), he taught at Ceylon, Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard as Professor of Anthropology (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo (1943–) is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard (Ph.D. under Masatoshi Nagatomi). He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS/University of London (c. 1968–1976), and Yale University.

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, and served as assistant professor (1959), associate professor (1963), and department chair (1967) at UCLA.
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, earning his Ph.D. under Alex Wayman around 1966–1970.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington. He held positions at Washington, Berkeley, Copenhagen, Bukkyo University, the University of Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak (1884–1962) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Leopold von Schroeder, Richard Simon, Adolf Kaegi, Antoine Meillet, Louis Finot, Sylvain Lévi, Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, and Andrzej Gawroński, and served as Professor at the University of Lviv (1928–1941).

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie. He held research posts at Stockholm, KTH, and Gävle, with visiting appointments at Virginia and UC Berkeley.

Stefan Mario Maul (1958–) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Göttingen and habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin, where he was an assistant. In 1995 he became Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University.

Stefan Mladenov (1880–1963) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Sofia, Vienna under Paul Kretschmer, Saint Petersburg under Baudouin de Courtenay, and Charles University (Ph.D.). He later served as PD, associate professor, and full professor at Sofia University.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and director of the Centre for the Study of Religion and Culture in Asia at the University of Groningen (c. 2013–2020) and later joined SOAS.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Ca' Foscari University under Alfredo Cadonna, and held posts at Soka University, Ca' Foscari, and the University of Oxford as Yehan Numata Professor (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll (1977–) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich, where he later worked as an assistant (2008–2015), before becoming Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Steingrímur Bjarnason Thorsteinsson (1831–1913) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík and the University of Copenhagen, and later worked as a teacher (1872) and senior teacher (1895) at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík.
